recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If MnM wants additional rendered Timing examples or dosage-specific examples, handle that as a new example/editorial decision rather than as a missing FHIR-12881 correction.
issue_request: FHIR-12881 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core datatypes request asking MnM to clarify how Timing.repeat.count works with frequency and period; the resolution said count is total repetitions across the timing duration and not the number of periods.
initial_application: Git history shows the substantive application in 0c1a713d764220d65de7203f9ccb1723a94ae7c7, '#1281 - note about use of Timing.repeat.count', with git-svn-id build@12467. That commit changed the Timing.repeat.count definition from 'A total count of the desired number of repetitions' to 'A total count of the desired number of repetitions across the duration of the entire timing specification'.
additional_context: Timing is active and normative in source/fhir.ini. Current source/datatypes/timing.xml preserves the total-count wording and the neighboring frequency and period definitions distinguish repetitions within a period from the total schedule count. The 2017 Zulip implementer thread supports count as event/dose count, and later FHIR-16986 preserved the total-count wording while adding countMax lower-bound semantics. Related FHIR-16986 and FHIR-15839 audits are already present on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the current authoritative source already answers the count-versus-period ambiguity; adding another example now would be redundant with the definition and adjacent frequency/period guidance.
